solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After onset of winter their nuts shrivel up

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of winter is used
nuts means crazy, so the letters of their are scrambled

explanation.surface: In winter some plants' nuts dry and shrivel.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is for a plant to dry out, shrink and wrinkle, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Children's publication is certain to lack one of the 3 Rs

indicators.note: to lack something is to go without it, so a letter is taken out of the word for certain

parts.note: certain means sure
the three Rs of basic schooling are reading, writing and arithmetic, all with the sound R; here the letter R

explanation.surface: A children's magazine is sure to skip one of the basics of schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works both ways: issue means offspring, and an issue is one number of a periodical such as a comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for offspring and also one printed number of a magazine.

clue.text: Hot oil sprinkled twice over river for masses

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: sprinkled means scattered about, so these letters are mixed up
twice means the word oil is taken two times over

parts.note: taken as written
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: Hot oil is sprinkled over food in a dish feeding the masses by an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprinkled' mixes the two copies of OIL with PO to make OIPOLLOI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek phrase means the many, the common people or ordinary crowd.

clue.text: Keep soldiers in check and Parisian in bucket

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: An officer keeps troops under control while a Frenchman is out in the downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue holds a second complete wordplay: 'and Parisian' is ET, French for and, put 'in bucket', RAIN (to bucket is to pour), also making R-ET-AIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to continue to possess it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: What hooker does to get pan cleaner

definitions.text: What hooker does to get pan cleaner

parts.words: What hooker does to get pan cleaner
parts.note: in rugby the hooker in the scrum faces the opposing pack; pan is slang for face, and a cosmetic mask cleans it

explanation.surface: Someone cleaning a cooking pan, or a rugby forward at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooker is a rugby forward in the middle of the front row of the scrum, so faces the other side's pack; 'pan' is old slang for face.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic paste spread on and left to dry is used to cleanse the skin of the face.

clue.text: I found horns struggling with time? Yes, time

indicators.note: struggling suggests things in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone caught by the horns wrestles against the clock, then concedes time is the issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'time', after 'Yes', is the definition; the first is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Relativity treats time as an extra dimension added to the three spatial ones.

clue.text: Universal problem for baby clothes at hospital

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the baby's complaint wraps around the other letters

parts.note: colic is abdominal pain common in infants
taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital deals with an infant's problem with its clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun for baby garments but is a verb meaning wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic in its lower-case sense means all-embracing or wide-ranging in scope.

clue.text: Mike produces trousers and shoes

indicators.note: trousers is a verb meaning pockets or takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to pup is to give birth to young, so produces means pups
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Mike brings out a range of trousers and footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is the verb for pocketing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumps are light plimsolls or court shoes worn for dancing or sport.

clue.text: Officer wasted hysterical reaction to fear

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

indicators.note: hysterical means wildly out of control, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A drunk officer has a hysterical fit of fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Clammy perspiration breaking out from nervous dread is a classic bodily response to terror.

clue.text: Second string player's beginning to go off

indicators.note: the first letter of the player's title departs, so the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a bass guitarist or double bass player is a string player; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A backup musician's career start goes badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second string player' looks like one phrase for a reserve, but 'Second' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To second someone is to back them up or help them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Minutely prepared yet premature

indicators.note: prepared means made up or worked into shape, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Something got ready in fine detail yet too early.
explanation.definitionFit: Untimely describes something happening too soon or before its proper time.

clue.text: Epicure boss of 22 captured during robbery

indicators.note: the boss is caught in the middle of the robbery, so placed within its letters

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
the mob at 22-down is headed by a don

explanation.surface: A gang boss is arrested mid-robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure devotes themselves to fine food and pleasure, as a pleasure-seeker does.

clue.text: Extract of Ulysses Bono returned to haunt

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the run of letters reads backwards
an extract is a passage taken from within the words

explanation.surface: A passage from Joyce's novel, read out by the U2 singer, keeps coming back to him.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in 'ULYSSES BONO' is SSESBO, which 'returned' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt someone's mind is to preoccupy them constantly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Dental examination?

parts.note: a spoken exam, a viva, is an examination using the mouth, as a dentist's check is

explanation.surface: A check-up at the dentist.
explanation.walkthrough: Dental suggests teeth, but the clue means a test answered by mouth rather than in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relating to the mouth and also a spoken test.

clue.text: Batsman whips Swedes, say

parts.note: Joe Root is a leading England Test cricket batsman
riding crops are short whips

explanation.surface: A cricketer thrashes some Scandinavians.
explanation.walkthrough: Swedes are not Scandinavians here but the root vegetable (rutabaga in the US).
explanation.definitionFit: Swedes are an example of vegetables grown for their edible underground part.

clue.text: Short day, still short, is getting shorter

parts.note: D is the short form of day

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: still air is windless

explanation.surface: On a brief, calm winter day, daylight keeps diminishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to diminish gradually, so the verb matches becoming smaller.

clue.text: Scary sign for island divers?

indicators.note: divers is an old word for various or diverse, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A warning notice for scuba divers around an island, perhaps about sharks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' looks like swimmers but works as the old adjective for assorted.
explanation.definitionFit: A shark's back fin cutting the water is the frightening signal swimmers dread.

clue.text: Leaves course meetings about a quarter to 6

indicators.note: about means around, so the meetings surround the other letters

parts.note: dates are social or romantic meetings
E for east is one of the four quarters of the compass
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A schedule of appointments set at a quarter to six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter to 6' reads as a time but gives E then VI.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to stray from a set route or norm.

clue.text: In which ELO music is played?

definitions.text: In which ELO music is played?

indicators.note: played suggests letters performed in a fresh arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking where the Electric Light Orchestra gives a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: ELO, the 1970s rock band, could play a large arena; the London Coliseum is a famous theatre and opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: A coliseum is a large stadium or theatre where performances such as rock concerts take place.

clue.text: Assess area covered by Irish transmitter

indicators.note: the area is placed under cover of the broadcaster, so it goes inside

parts.note: RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster

explanation.surface: Judging how much ground an Irish radio mast reaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to evaluate or judge its value, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Criminal fails to hide first of crimes from Revenue

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one letter goes within the others
criminal means wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged
first of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A crook fails to conceal his first offence from the tax authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges FAILS into FISAL, and C goes inside to make FISCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal describes matters of public money and taxation, what derives from tax revenue.

clue.text: Sulphur affected international seafood

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
camp means mannered or affected in style

explanation.surface: A sulphur-tainted global shipment of seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustine tails, often breaded and fried, a seafood dish.

clue.text: Mob always fraternised in America initially

definitions.text: Mob always fraternised in America initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: The Mob always mixed socially in the United States, at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian-American crime syndicate is known simply as the Mob.

clue.text: Pest lives in shade

indicators.note: in places the word for lives inside the shade

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or colour
is, as in exists, stands for lives

explanation.surface: An insect lives in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pest' suggests a bug, but here it is an irritating person or thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is a person or thing that annoys, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Tea bags in service

indicators.note: bags means grabs or holds, so the word for tea encloses the other letters

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tea bags being used in a dinner service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' looks like teabags but is a verb meaning takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea or dinner service is a set of porcelain crockery.

clue.text: At entrance to church it often gets scattered

definitions.text: At entrance to church it often gets scattered

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter
scattered means strewn about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is strewn about at a church door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance to' gives C, and 'scattered' turns IT OFTEN into ONFETTI; the whole clue also describes the wedding custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bits of coloured paper are thrown over bride and groom outside the church after a wedding.

clue.text: Fines put in money box

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the fines go within the money

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money
F is the abbreviation for fine, so two fines give FF

explanation.surface: Fines paid are dropped into a money box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money box' looks like one phrase, but 'box' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden case for burying the dead is a box, informally.

clue.text: Ruby, for example, popular with idiots

parts.note: an ass is an idiot, so two idiots make ASS ASS
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A gem, or a woman named Ruby, is liked by fools.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ruby shot Lee Harvey Oswald, the assassin of President Kennedy, in 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ruby killed Oswald, so he is an example of a political killer.

clue.text: Carriage left with a uniform

parts.note: with can mean and, as in fish with chips
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A coach abandoned along with an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.
